## Evidence and cause boundary

The actual full2 failure at runtime_delivery_continuation_tests.rs:351 returned `unsafe_storage` with the owner-only/not-linked message while `maintain_phase_observations` wrapped source sealing. It occurred before the validation-retry fixture was entered. The log does not identify the file or metadata values; this artifact does not assert the exact failing leaf.

A concrete reachable production race is visible statically: ordinary and active provider observation reconstruction read `ControlHost::operations()` outside Control, while source sealing and other admitted work replace protected receipts under Control. `PrivateDir::open_file` obtains a descriptor then verifies its link count. A legitimate atomic rename can unlink that descriptor between open and metadata, yielding nlink zero and the observed unsafe_storage class. ReceiptStore::all separately enumerates and reads; it provides no synchronization itself. The observation-maintenance wrapper preserves its first real refresh failure and can return that failure even after the phase settles.

The second full2 chain publication failure (`observation_unavailable`, latest reconciliation did not complete) remains independently unresolved here. This patch neither asserts its cause nor adds a fixture barrier, timeout extension or success retry.

`reconstruction_receipts` enters Control serialization once and reads one owned Vec of actual protected receipts. The existing ordinary host-comment and classification reconstructors consume that same slice outside Control. The same Vec is forwarded through `refresh_active`, so every active projection in the refresh uses the same receipt epoch. The two reconstruction helpers are now read-only functions of supplied receipt data; their exact verification bodies and native publication stability comparisons are preserved.

`restore_classifications` had exactly two callers, both in observations.rs. `restore_host_comment_ids` also has exactly those ordinary/active callers. Both original helper bodies use no further Control gates or provider calls. The new capture runs after the first native read, outside an existing Control gate; all provider awaits remain outside Control. The later `apply_corrective_publications` already runs in the existing final serialized publication callback, so its independent current receipt read remains unchanged and safe from these writers. Public `ControlHost::operations` is unchanged because many callers already hold Control. PrivateDir, ownership, link, schema, record-size, source, native, grant and current-authority validation are unchanged.

The snapshot is historical data, not an authorization token. A newly acknowledged publication after capture cannot be used to authenticate the current reconstruction; the next actual refresh can capture it. Existing fail-closed publication/config/freshness/final corrective gates remain in force. No synthetic timestamps, copied success flags or implicit replays are introduced.

- `observations::receipt_tests::reconstruction_snapshot_waits_for_actual_receipt_replacement_gate`: real protected Control admission and effect Sent receipt. A genuine complete_effect callback holds Control before the actual replacement; a concurrent call to the production snapshot helper must not return during that gate, then must contain the exact complete Acknowledged receipt after release. Both actual threads join, the local component permit is retired, and the previously captured Sent snapshot remains unchanged. The 100 ms negative receive asserts exclusion; 10-second channel deadlines prevent an unbounded test barrier. No process or native model is asserted.

# Declared protocol EOF design — independent review

**Result: feasible as a diagnostic-only extension that retains Incomplete.** No architecture blocker was found, but the concrete integration constraints below must be preserved. This is a design review, not validation of an implemented transport-end producer. No source change, Cargo/test, native process or provider call occurred.

Reviewed full DESIGN and TEST-MATRIX at `/private/tmp/kegari-declared-protocol-eof-design-v1`, design SHA `9a0a73c0f023080c7f66e4f2619c37e08d6fc29b029cf85c693e6049adf90107`, FILES `177f3eaecb0ed5b1a8f55ed98fa084aae2ad6cbbf87db5df3041d8ceba0f431a`. All three listed members verified. INPUTS preserves the original design source identities and the exact supporting source read now. Four files have since acquired the previously reviewed observer-v1 bytes; the runtime/deadline/worker-run supporting files still match their original design hashes. The held observer union remains the reviewed dependency, not an EOF implementation.

## Required concrete integration constraints

1. **Retain policy before rejecting unknown turn data.** `SessionState::block_provider` binds the exact current thread but deliberately does not require an already-known turn. `notification` observes turn policy before ordinary turn identity rejection. A tail classifier must retain that same-bound policy even when it refuses a new/unknown turn; it must not accept `turn/started` as new work. Unknown or foreign ordinary output stays diagnostic/conflicting. A pure ProtocolObserver callback alone cannot persist the real runtime hold.

   Use an ownership-bound blocked-session checkpoint callback, preserving the original pending method. Do not route that denial observation only through AuditedHost's lease-first `observe_session`: the original deadline can expire after a frame was read or during storage, and then the lease check would prevent retention of an already observed hold. The real ScopedWorker/RuntimeCoordinator checkpoint validates its registered operation/contract and retains the hold without granting work. Limit this callback to genuinely blocked/input-required candidates; generic checkpoint on an ordinary completed session can call `finish_proposals`. Ordinary tail frames remain diagnostic until the existing final checkpoint.

2. **Retain late interaction requirements as well as policy notifications.** `service_request` currently sets `input_required` for command/file/permission approvals, legacy exec/apply approvals, user-input requests and MCP elicitation. The no-write tail must not use that dispatcher, but it should retain the exact bound deny-only interaction observation instead of merely recording UnsupportedRequestChannel and allowing the earlier completed outcome to survive. Unbound/foreign input is explicit, not adopted. Add the real decoder/component case alongside late policy; no tools, replies or grants are created.

3. **Establish the thread only after all actual start validation.** `start_thread` assigns `state.thread_id` before `instruction_sources(&response)?`. Failure can therefore leave a tentative ID. Emit `ThreadEstablished` only after every original response/instruction-source check succeeds; final AdapterInventory or generic `bind(state)` must not retrospectively establish that tentative thread or relabel earlier bootstrap data as bound. Test instruction-source failure with an otherwise matching ID.

4. **Separate the exact admitted request budget from the absolute cutoff.** `RuntimeLiveAuthority` captures `remaining.as_secs().max(1)` and its acquire method requires exact equality with `LiveRequest.max_seconds`. Recomputing remaining inside `run_live_trial_until` after file validation can cross a second boundary and falsely reject an unchanged admission. Carry the same original request-budget Duration and the original absolute deadline as distinct inputs (or one private value containing both). The request uses the former; all model/collection/tail waits use the latter. No deadline renewal and no weakening of authority equality. Config acknowledged constraints 1, 3 and 4 during review; the interaction and byte-accounting notes were also sent for implementation.

## Smallest safe adapter shapes

- Factor existing helper bodies; keep ordinary public entrypoints delegating to the original denial behavior. A private borrowed observation-only denial wrapper may forward bounded diagnostics but never call the worker's tool executor. Thread it through all metadata helpers and the existing watchdog interrupt, not only startup. Do not send a new interrupt merely for observation.
- Count every actual parsed frame at the reader boundary, including matched/unmatched responses and no-state notifications. Metadata response contents stay private to existing validation. A narrow matched-Turn projection carries actual request ID/method/requested thread/inline mode and provisional validation status; do not expose full account/config/model objects to a raw logging sink. Only the existing successful helper checks can promote its attribution. A response does not itself complete the session or clear an unknown request.
- `TransportRead::CleanEof` may originate only from the original reader returning zero after the pending queue is consumed and decoder.finish succeeds. Keep a sticky per-client end/error state; neither a generic process_exit string nor a clean owned termination constructs it. A private non-deserializable diagnostic result should remain distinct from native exit/retirement APIs.
- Frame/byte accounting must state its unit. RpcMessage currently discards original encoded length. Re-serialization is not exact wire-byte accounting (whitespace, CRLF, queued frames and residual decoder bytes differ). Preserve original reader/decoded-frame counts or explicitly distinguish and bound actual bytes plus decoded payload. Queued messages must be charged too. Conservative resource refusal is acceptable; successful truncation is not.
- Tail processing must have no pipe write, tool invocation, generic dispatcher, thread creation or result adoption. Use an allowlisted candidate-state classifier: only real denial/policy/input-required state can persist early. Exact duplicates may be reconciled; unsolicited responses, unknown work and conflicts remain gaps. Final outcome/pending/usage/checkpoint and lifecycle observation must use reconciled state while retaining the original execution error.

## Shutdown and time boundary

The existing reader/decoder/queue remains owned after terminate, so a separate bounded diagnostic read is technically possible without another reader or task. The owner must remain the same actual evaluator task. A failed/draining model callback is not joined merely because its borrow ends; it keeps its existing unknown hold and cannot yield complete coverage. Termination failure and actual EOF are independent facts.

Use the same original deadline before polling a queued-ready frame, after synchronous capture, and before recording a timely clean-end fact; timeout_at alone must not let an already-ready queue/EOF bypass an expired cutoff. Stop collecting on time/resource failure, keep incomplete, and continue the existing actual cleanup/settlement. No Control/RuntimeState lock spans reads or process joins. Final durable report persistence remains after work/collection classification and must not reopen that window.

## Limits

The proposed 17 component cases are useful, but remain unimplemented/unrun at design review. Duplex EOF establishes only parser/transport observation. Actual owned process, registry, finalization, policy-checkpoint failure and cancellation races still need appropriate runtime evidence; no synthetic native completion is acceptable. Clean EOF does not establish descendant exit, network/read/effect completeness, non-disclosure, acceptance or E07 success. This increment must retain Incomplete, unchanged scorer/fixture semantics and legacy unknown data.

# Declared transport v2 independent review

Summary: One concrete bootstrap-output preservation gap and one smaller contradictory diagnostic label remain in held v2. No additional material authority, ownership or EOF-boundary issue was found in the bounded static review. No Cargo, compilation, tests, native/provider calls or source edits were performed.

Exact held artifact: `/private/tmp/kegari-declared-protocol-transport-v2`; FILES `7461b865758fd0db14af547053c0fdfd62fe92cf791645b02cf9b767feccc5de`, patch `1a4726594db8d65e3141677d81d9a9a8909700dff1a8b6134bd52c537db6aa47`, COMPOSED `40a3bf82fab5063a155bb75a34e889a5de97eae3b65d83216ceb4c283bcdf946`. All 47 manifest members and 11 incremental base/draft identities were independently checked. The full union contains 20 paths. Original artifacts remain unchanged.

## Findings

**T-1 — Completed output in the tentative thread/start window is discarded.** `RpcClient::request` sends notifications through `checkpoint_notification` whenever `Some(state)` is supplied; thread/start supplies its tentative SessionState. This emits CompletedItem/TerminalTurn even before the new ThreadEstablished event. Both corresponding `ProtocolCapture::observe` arms in `codex_observation.rs` return immediately when `bind()` sees `!established`. Thus a genuine item/completed arriving before the thread/start response loses its agentMessage text, while the equivalent initialize/no-state notification and response-contained turn are preserved as operation-only unbound records. The explicit UnestablishedThread issue and always-incomplete state prevent a false completeness claim, but they do not preserve the actually received output requested by this increment. This was independently confirmed after Config raised the exact post-HOLD question.

Recommended narrow correction in a separate immutable follow-up: project completed agentMessage text into the existing operation-only unbound channel only when the collector has never established a thread. Preserve UnestablishedThread and rejection/malformed diagnostics; do not fill bound message/turn inventories or adopt the tentative thread. Do not fall back when an already-established binding changes or a foreign thread arrives. Use a real duplex thread/start exchange with a notification before its response, rather than only injecting the collector event.

**T-2 — Request-count record retains an obsolete categorical tail label.** `codex_observation.rs` records `transport_tail: "unobserved"` in AdapterInventory even after a separate actual CleanEof fact has been retained. This does not grant authority, but the two retained diagnostics contradict each other. Replace the count record's label with a neutral statement such as `count_does_not_prove_tail`; the distinct typed end observation remains the only source of EOF facts.

Both findings were sent to root and Config. Held v2 was not changed. Any follow-up needs its own hash-bound delta review.

## Reviewed boundaries with no further finding

Bootstrap and watchdog wrappers forward observation while denying calls and keeping their prior no-op session checkpoint behavior. Only the private declared IndependentReview opt-in records raw data; ordinary ScopedWorkers remain disabled. ThreadEstablished occurs after complete original response/instruction-source/tool validation. Matched-response projection uses the actual matched request, requested thread and inline review identity, and does not adopt a completion or create a worker capability.

The tail pass retains the same original RpcClient reader, decoder and queued messages, is single-use, and performs no tool dispatch, response write, turn start or uncertain-request reconciliation. CleanEof originates from an actual zero-byte read after successful decoder.finish. Residual/new wire bytes and re-encoded queued-frame bytes have separately stated finite bounds; partial/poisoned input and overflow do not become EOF. All enabled observations keep CoverageNotQualified and remain incomplete or a stronger failure state.

The actual runtime passes its original absolute deadline separately from the unchanged remaining-duration authority request. Tail collection cannot borrow cleanup grace; the existing owned outer settlement remains authoritative. Late exact-thread policy extraction occurs before ordinary unknown-turn refusal. Known-turn approval/input requests retain input_required. Both use the actual worker checkpoint without the lease-first wrapper; `finish_proposals` refuses intervention and input_required, so these denial checkpoints cannot publish proposals. Final state/outcome/checkpoint occurs after the tail, preserving earlier failures and actual cleanup obligations. EOF supplies no process, joined-worker, remote-effect or native exit authority.

The twelve authored component tests use actual duplex/parser/reader/storage mechanisms with explicitly synthetic session/catalog data, and remain unrun. Protected report roundtrip coverage is extended without a scorer/fixture migration. Current-source composition must preserve root's already-installed needless-borrow lint correction. No native containment, full-channel completeness, canary non-disclosure, E07 success or human qualification is established.

## Distinct publication interleaving, independent of receipt-file failure

refresh_inner takes a first native projection and saves publication_revision,
then reconstructs publication and host-comment references. If these change it
performs a second native read; any comment identity/body/writer change causes
`unstable_observation / authority publications changed during reconstruction`
(observations.rs352–389,449–479). refresh records that error as observation_failed
before returning. The fixture poller intentionally swallows this exact error,
leaving gates unavailable until another successful actual refresh.

One of the two origin publications can become visible between those reads. A
subsequent current_gate callback for the same or second mutation then sees the
cached failure and emits precisely the observed generic error. No file corruption,
receipt race, wrong accepted token or relaxed authority is needed for this
interleaving. Production refusal is conservative and expected for an unstable
observation; this fixture's unconditional publication unwrap may be assuming a
stable interval it has not arranged.

## Shared receipt-race path also remains possible

The same refresh calls restore_host_comment_ids, which invokes control.operations
before rebuilding the current native host comment IDs (observations.rs482–487).
A receipt-inventory unsafe_storage error at that point propagates out of
refresh_inner and is recorded as observation_failed. The next current_gate then
emits the same generic observation_unavailable. That is exactly why the generic
panic does not establish a separate production defect.

No `fixture observation poll failed` appears in the captured log, whereas the
poller deliberately emits no panic for unstable_observation. This is consistent
with the distinct publication path, but is not sufficient to exclude a
background task timing/output-capture edge. Treat it as supporting context only.

## Minimal next diagnostic, before changing barriers

1. In the publication loop retain the ordinal, purpose and original request UUID.
   Wrap only the existing `move || current_gate(&admitted_gate)` error to attach
   those values and `observations.health()` to the same error. Do this in the
   callback, where ProviderBroker already holds Control; health is a cache read,
   so it does not reacquire Control. That captures the latched cause before a
   later successful refresh can overwrite it. Preserve the original code,
   message, callback and all refusal behavior.
2. Log the poll error code/message (including swallowed unstable_observation)
   before its existing match; keep its behavior unchanged. The public mutation
   failure should also print its ordinal/UUID to distinguish first versus second
   publication and reserve versus final-gate failures if a callback counter is
   retained as diagnostic data.
3. Inspect the health cause and actual phase/result of only those existing
   publication operation receipts after failure. No refresh or reconciliation
   should be inserted merely to erase the cause. Do not infer causation from a
   passing rerun.

If the captured cause is unsafe_storage, evaluate Codex's exact reader repair;
there is no justification here for a publication fix. If it is unstable_observation,
the narrow fixture option is an explicitly bounded stable publication interval
using the existing poll barrier and real complete native refreshes, preserving
all current gates and owner receipts. Its exact placement should be chosen only
after the diagnostic. No recommendation to widen the barrier over assembly,
lengthen TTL, add arbitrary sleep, or alter production publication selection.

A future deterministic reproduction could coordinate the actual fixture comment
read/write callbacks so a real publication occurs between reconstruction passes,
then assert that health records unstable_observation and gates refuse until a
real successful refresh. This is a proposed regression, not authored or executed
coverage in this read-only task.
